claims.text: In 2021-2025, age-standardised cancer mortality in North Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county was 4.0% below the national level (ratio 0.96, 95% interval 0.933-0.988), about 35.5 fewer deaths a year than its age structure predicts.

Waiting time of over 3 months since assessment of the need for treatment for a non-emergency appointment with a primary health care doctor in outpatient care, % of completed appointments: North Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county is at 8.23 (three-year mean to 2025) against 1.7 nationally.

Patients waiting over 6 months during the year for access to specialised health care per 10 000 inhabitants: North Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county is at 81.07 (three-year mean to 2025) against 36 nationally.
Among the stages that public data can measure, the earliest one where North Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county is clearly worse than the country is first contact and primary care access.

Time from referral to diagnosis and from diagnosis to first treatment is not published by county for any cancer, so the Goal 3 indicator "patients access treatment within the established target times" cannot be checked from open data.

Proportion of women invited to cervical cancer screening (smear test) who attended, %: 73.6% against the 80% target. HPV self-sampling kits for cervical screening non-attenders is expected to add 1.5-4.5 percentage points, closing about 47% of the gap.

Proportion of invited to colorectal cancer screening who attended, %: 76.9% against the 80% target. Reminder and multilingual re-invitation for colorectal screening is expected to add 1.5-3.13 percentage points, closing about 96% of the gap.
First step for every county: Add first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publish county-level medians quarterly.
